scope: Every Python rule in the 200-rule registry at main 3d848ea71f4ee1b4c2c7469e8bfebf8f8e036e07 plus six rules added by this change; source-level applicability review, not an assertion of identical enforcement across languages. Updated through Python 1.101.1 at main 8be04fdae02f3c6e77009ce100d4c39ded3936b6 with the additional SARJ556 review and subsequent existing-rule semantic refinements; the original review and its 13 TypeScript rule additions remain historical facts.

decisionDefinitions.existing-local: Existing source-semantic TypeScript rule owns the stated bounded concern.
decisionDefinitions.existing-upstream: Maintained upstream rule owns the portable source form; availability does not imply every consumer enables the same preset.
decisionDefinitions.native-semantics: JavaScript/TypeScript syntax or runtime has materially different behavior; use native contracts instead of copying the Python detector.
decisionDefinitions.new-local: A bounded new TypeScript rule provides the identified portable source relationship.
decisionDefinitions.extended-local: An existing TypeScript rule gained the missing portable relationship.
decisionDefinitions.new-upstream: This change enables a maintained upstream rule.
decisionDefinitions.python-api: The Python rule's concrete failure depends on a Python runtime API absent from native JavaScript.
decisionDefinitions.framework-specific: The owning Python framework has no common TypeScript API to which this detector can be safely translated.
decisionDefinitions.architecture-review: The general concern is useful in review, but no equivalent source proof is supplied by the supported TypeScript runtime; names alone are deliberately insufficient.
decisionDefinitions.shared-sql-policy: The shared SQL engine owns the portable SQL concern; embedded driver/query-builder coverage is not implied.

rules.basis: ExitStack.callback has no JavaScript equivalent; async disposers use the native async-disposal protocol.
Python executor.shutdown(wait=True) is not a Node API; do not infer blocking behavior from arbitrary shutdown methods.
Calling JavaScript async functions eagerly starts their body; Python AsyncMock called-versus-awaited semantics do not transfer.
asyncio cancellation ownership is absent from native JavaScript promises; AbortSignal and ChildProcess lifecycles need API-specific evidence.
Promises have no native cancel operation or asyncio.Task join lifecycle.
Psycopg/PostgreSQL execution-shape review is driver-specific. Arbitrary TypeScript SQL strings are not proof of an executable PostgreSQL query.
Vitest's expected-failure tests already fail when the callback unexpectedly passes; there is no pytest strict=False equivalent.
FastAPI route decorators/status declarations have no direct Next/server-action analogue; guessing a framework's response policy would overreach.
Typed documentation sections and lexical JSDoc restatement are already covered; JavaScript JSDoc type contracts remain valid.
Existing documentation rules own repeated return contracts.
JavaScript has one catch clause; duplicated typed exception clauses are not syntax it supports.
Python's closed builtin regex/string helper proof does not establish equivalence of arbitrary JavaScript regex callbacks or Unicode string operations; no general duplicate-helper ban is added.
Vitest each/for literal case duplication is already covered; pytest fixture params are framework-specific.
Existing exact action-narration rule.
subprocess count-result ownership and Python fallback contracts differ from Node child-process streams; no name-only probe detector is added.
Test-double ownership depends on consumer architecture; TypeScript structural inline collaborators can be valid and no generic fake-class placement rule is justified.
FastAPI Router.build/response_model metadata is not a TypeScript framework API; existing service contracts cover the portable class boundary.
FastAPI OpenAPI declaration requirements cannot be imposed on Next server actions or every JavaScript router.
Existing parsed source-oracle rule.
Typed schema defaults reject incompatible types; refinement-specific invalid defaults still require runtime schema tests rather than claiming full Pydantic parity.
TypeScript collaborators can use typed vi.fn and structural interfaces; unsafe casts are already checked. Python spec=True is not a JavaScript mock option.
Existing named return-contract rules.
JavaScript Math.min/Math.max propagate NaN regardless of argument order; Python builtin min/max's order-dependent hiding does not occur.
Source-proven fetch/native Response status tests now require an exact status oracle instead of merely excluding a 5xx.
The shared SQL engine already owns transactional analytical-query policy for SQL input; do not claim that this automatically covers every TypeScript query builder.
Any-valued record annotations and propagation already have maintained upstream owners.
Promises can be awaited repeatedly; caching a promise does not reproduce Python's single-use coroutine-object defect.
Existing phase-label control plus new general maintained-test prose policy.
Direct source-proven mutable object writes with returned values are covered; arbitrary Zod preprocess callbacks retain separate API-specific semantics.
Existing suppression policy and local rationale controls own blanket disables.
Typed object/rest parameter contracts replace Python **kwargs; broad any interfaces are already rejected.
Existing comment-cruft owner.
Pydantic alias validation configuration has no Zod equivalent: Zod object keys are declared directly.
pytest's implicit conftest loading is absent from JavaScript modules; ordinary fixture imports can be valid.
Existing typed primitive/array predicate checks.
JSDoc restatement owner; runtime JavaScript type documentation is preserved.
Existing credentialed wildcard CORS control.
FastAPI path-decorator grammar does not apply to Next actions or every Node router; no API ownership is inferred from route names alone.
Portable typed-outcome guidance is supported by exhaustive typed contracts; name-only exception classes cannot establish expected domain control flow in JavaScript.
Shared SQL engine owns database functions and triggers; JavaScript query-builder calls require driver-specific review.
TypeScript environment access already has a settings boundary; Pydantic BaseSettings environment field defaults do not have one common JavaScript settings API.
Direct borrowed-object field deletion in result-returning functions is covered. JavaScript property deletion remains valid in explicit void commands; a blanket Python del-statement ban is not copied.
Ignored Zod safeParse outcome is covered; arbitrary application result unions still need an explicit effect contract.
Detects ignored schema parse outputs that visibly normalize/default/coerce/transform input.
Existing JSDoc type-restatement controls.
Typed field access and schema boundaries cover known contracts; there is no shared Pydantic-model-or-dict runtime in Zod.
JavaScript exports are syntax, not a separately maintained __all__ list. Banning exports would remove module contracts.
Duplicate exports are compiler/parser-owned; no mutable __all__ manifest exists.
Zod has no named decorator-based field validator registry; arbitrary repeated callbacks can differ by closure/context.
Existing 5xx exception leakage rule.
Existing syntax-aware cognitive complexity control.
Deprecated FastAPI on_event has no same API in JavaScript.
Native JavaScript suppression controls own the analogous escape hatch.
Python underscore module names are conventions, not JavaScript access modifiers. Native private/export boundaries should not be replaced by spelling inference.
Existing fixed-sleep test control.
Existing polling/sleep controls cover supported JavaScript forms; not every scheduled Node timer is a busy loop.
Python requests/status-code branch folding requires a particular HTTP-client protocol; arbitrary JavaScript integer branches are not proof of HTTP status handling.
Readonly writes have compiler ownership; no Pydantic frozen after-validator lifecycle exists in Zod.
Existing generic module naming rule.
Typed reflection is already checked. JavaScript in/hasOwn is necessary for sound unknown-value narrowing and cannot be banned as hasattr.
Existing dependency architecture rules cover owned service contracts; arbitrary default constructor values need not be application-setting fallbacks.
Existing native Zod interval owners.
JavaScript static module loading is explicit; injecting a loader is not proof that a loader's bundler/runtime contract is redundant.
Direct writes of locally declared mutable object parameter fields in result-returning functions.
Existing dynamic execution and library-load policies own JavaScript source execution; Python interpreter argv strings are not JavaScript source.
Native property/alias and explained suppression policies cover the portable boundary; Python parameter snake_case is not JavaScript naming.
Existing typed invalid bypass and write controls.
Native callback signatures check annotated return types; custom unvalidated parser bypasses have an existing dedicated owner.
Loguru exc_info is a Python-only logging API option.
Loguru formatting conventions do not apply to Node loggers, whose formatting APIs differ.
Typed value-object shape fabrication is already checked; Pydantic BaseModel isinstance identity has no general Zod object identity equivalent.
Array-valued transforms track primitive array inputs/aliases, direct writes and native mutators; void commands/fresh copies stay valid.
Zod validators are not resolved by nested-class decorator ownership.
Portable substitutability has explicit owners; optional input-to-default normalization is valid JavaScript and not necessarily a hidden dependency resolver.
Existing embedded SQL OFFSET control.
Existing typed false-branch predicate soundness control.
TypeScript database drivers usually return named records; unnamed fixed result records already have an owner. Psycopg row_factory is Python-specific.
Existing fixed tuple-return record owner.
Unused bindings have upstream ownership; proving vi mock configuration cannot affect execution requires a separate mock protocol/control-flow proof, not Python Mock transfer.
Existing injected SQL ownership rule recognizes supported Node database/query-builder forms.
Shared SQL engine owns UUID defaults; native JS UUID policy is separate and is not claimed to enforce PostgreSQL UUIDv7 in arbitrary embedded queries.
Reuse source-proven database fixture instances. Raw SQL can be legitimate integration assertions; no blanket Node-driver call ban is inferred without that fixture/driver contract.
Existing raw-source oracle control.
Recording-only collaborators can be valid isolated TypeScript unit tests; the Python PostgreSQL-backed test-store architecture is not a universal Node fake ban.
Stable one-use local aliases forwarded into matching object shorthand fields are now reviewed; snapshots and typed contracts remain valid.
Maintained export and module-boundary rules own JavaScript re-exports; Python sys.modules replacement has no ES module equivalent.
SQL alias removal is dialect/quoted-identifier-sensitive; this task does not claim a regex equivalent for arbitrary JavaScript SQL strings.
Existing structured-string duplication owner.
Existing substantial sibling test-body duplication owner.

The Python rule proves repeated stdlib PRNG sampling. JavaScript Math.random replacement, library seeds and test generators need an explicit runner/PRNG proof; a name-only random ban would reject valid stochastic contracts.
Existing prose/domain reuse rules cover known TS domains; a Zod schema description can legitimately differ from TS literal declarations.
Existing restated-comment owner.
Existing secret/whole-body logging owner.
Existing embedded SQL projection owner.
Pydantic settings classes are identifiable runtime types; arbitrary JavaScript Config-named objects do not prove settings ownership.
Existing primitive-element Array.isArray predicate checks.
Added named local record guards that promise required data fields from only typeof-object/null checks.
FastAPI APIRouter prefix and empty-path semantics do not transfer to all JavaScript routers.
Existing constant assertion owners.
Existing repeated string accumulator owner.
JavaScript has no intrinsic asyncio cancellation exception; AbortError ownership varies by runtime and should not be inferred from an arbitrary error name.
Existing first-party method/module replacement policy covers supported substitutions.
Existing numeric/unit narration owner.

Psycopg UniqueViolation/constraint metadata is a driver-specific contract; Node database clients expose different error protocols and arbitrary message matching is not proven to be uniqueness control flow.
Zod object schema keys and callback typing replace Pydantic named field-validator decorators; no decorator field registry exists.
Existing prose/doc section controls preserve executable JS JSDoc.
Maintained unused replacement-return checks own recognized native copy/transformation APIs.
Native unused parameter controls own JS/TS parameters; JavaScript has no Python keyword-only caller contract.
Existing unused binding/expression controls; explicit void expression can intentionally mark a promise/side-effect boundary and is not an underscore assignment.
Existing exact suppression explanation owner.
Rule explicitly includes raw request/response blob names, containers and supported serialization wrappers; not just credential fields.
FastAPI GET route work-verb semantics do not establish arbitrary JavaScript function or Next action behavior.
Opaque pytest IDs are not the same API as formatted Vitest table titles. Vitest has a maintained title validator, but it is not claimed as enabled or as proof of semantic case IDs.
An arbitrary mock-count ceiling is a review heuristic tied to the runner and collaborator boundaries; no duplicate count rule is introduced without equivalent protocol evidence.
Application-model joins require model/table ownership evidence. A general SQL JOIN ban in TypeScript would reject valid query-builder/relational operations.
Typed JavaScript mocks check callable signatures at compilation; Python autospec's runtime binding protocol has no identical vi option.
A same-name Node upsert_many method does not prove the transaction/result/duplicate policy of its scalar peer; retain architectural review rather than infer bulk equivalence.
Node drivers commonly return named records and Zod validates object values; Psycopg class_row/dict_row is a Python API.
Maintained native collection operations own applicable JS builder shapes; JavaScript has no Python comprehension syntax.
Existing timing-safe authenticator comparison owner.
Zod exposes declarative array parsing natively; arbitrary loops over schema.parse may intentionally attach per-item context and are not rewritten without a collection contract.
Static ES imports and dynamic library policy already own literal module loading.
Existing typed discriminated union owner.
Maintained template interpolation control.
Pydantic BaseSettings prefix fields have no single JavaScript configuration runtime; grouping arbitrary common-name object keys would be a naming-only source freeze.
Existing module constant immutability owner.
Existing injection/substitute ownership rules cover supported TS test replacement seams.
Third-party fake/emulator availability is service-specific, not derivable from JavaScript source alone.
Existing exhaustiveness owners.
Guarded Python exception match syntax does not transfer to instanceof catch branches; simple value dispatch already has an owner.
JavaScript has no structural pattern matching; only applicable repeated literal-value dispatch is promoted.
Existing repeated-value dispatch owner.
Existing static value hoisting owner.

Vitest supplies reversible process-state APIs, but the installed plugin has no prefer-vi-stub-global/prefer-vi-stub-env rules. Pytest monkeypatch ownership is not equivalent to automatic restoration of an arbitrary Vitest global mutation.
JavaScript's monotonic performance API differs from Python time module bindings; arbitrary Date.now timestamps can be legitimate wall-clock records.
String/JSON adapters have native type and generic-parser owners; do not rewrite arbitrary user decoder calls as Python str checks.
Existing nominal ID boundary owner.
Existing nullable collection contract owner.
Related optionals may describe independent states; TypeScript variants already have a supported discriminated-union owner rather than a universal object grouping mandate.
JavaScript groups fall-through case labels natively; Python OR patterns have no distinct JS syntax.
Existing bounded precise object contract controls; public/opaque object boundaries are preserved.
Psycopg executemany's result/transaction contract does not prove Node SQL-client batch equivalence.
Zod supplies its own JSON validator; the new generic-parser field-read rule preserves legitimate opaque JSON forwarding.
Existing dense object/projection assertion owner.
Source-proven supplied class fixture reuse for Vitest/Playwright-style fixture runners.
Reuse already supplied fixture objects; Python pool fixture discovery is not copied into Node by naming alone.
JavaScript has no fullmatch method. Python match/search end-anchor semantics require a different regex proof; maintained regexp rules retain JS-specific authority.
Required parameters are enforced when declared; optional/default parameters can be valid domain APIs, so no blanket default ban is ported.
Existing runtime boundary validation and sound-predicate controls.
Existing explicit unit/control-duration owners; arbitrary constants are not renamed solely from numeric values.
TypeScript natively supports polymorphic this; signatures may deliberately return a base contract, so no constructor-name-only rewrite is imposed.
Maintained JavaScript native Set disjointness owner.
TypeScript's chosen contract is Zod/literal domains, not Python StrEnum runtime objects.
Python collections.namedtuple factory has no same JS API; named return records already have an owner.
Python Typer parser metadata is not a generic Node CLI framework; selecting a JS CLI library is a library-policy task.
Typed record fields and focused JSON schemas cover the portable contract; legitimate dynamic Maps remain valid.
Pydantic settings field default-derived domain inference has no shared JavaScript settings runtime; TS catches declared type/default mismatch.
JavaScript permits assignment expressions already; a Python walrus-specific style rule would impose unrelated control-flow spelling.
JavaScript has no comprehension filter syntax; callback/helper invocation effects must not be treated as repeated pure calls without proof.
Python assignment-to-if spelling rule is not a distinct JavaScript operator feature; JS regex state also changes repeated-match semantics.
Python producer-loop walrus rewrite has no direct new JavaScript syntax requirement.
Imported membership arrays in Vitest tables require an independent literal-membership oracle; deliberate enum/registry sweeps stay valid.
Existing named return record rule covers fixed tuple fixture results; fixture callback data object shape remains framework-owned.
Explicit using/await using return escapes now have a source owner; awaited fixture-use lifecycle remains with typed promise checks.
Existing JSDoc lexical repetition owner.
Existing JSDoc lexical repetition owner.
Existing redundant prose owners; executable JSDoc type/import contracts are preserved.
Maintained unnecessary constructor/override forwarding control owns supported JS forms.
Existing case factoring plus newly reused supplied fixtures; JavaScript object literals are not Python keyword-argument calls.
Existing same-shape literal-call case factoring owner.
Supplied collaborator construction is now recognized for fixture reuse; arbitrary SUT constructors are not blanket banned.
Typed structural test doubles need not implement every interface member with raising placeholder bodies; the compiler owns declared compatibility.
Existing embedded insert replay-policy review owner.
jose verification must require exp or maxTokenAge; jsonwebtoken is already restricted in favor of jose.
Existing explicit substitute contract owner.
Psycopg connection transaction ownership cannot be translated to arbitrary Node clients by method names; supported SQL access still has an injected owner.
Existing explicit service boundary contract owner.
Tenacity retry sleep injection has no same Node API; timers and retry libraries require their actual cancellation/ownership contracts.
JavaScript has no keyword-only parameter syntax. Role-separated nominal types already protect known ID swaps; arbitrary positional primitive signatures are not renamed automatically.
Pydantic-settings NoDecode is Python runtime metadata, not a Zod parsing option.
Existing consumer-owned port rule.
Native compiler signatures check known object/callback fields; dynamic any factories already have upstream owners.
Source-proven private readonly concrete dependencies with one declared local interface now prefer that existing interface.
Existing source-proven external JSON validation rule.
Focused JSON field contracts and unsound shallow named-record guards are covered; legitimate dictionary indexing remains valid.
Existing runtime validation plus focused known-field parsing; no FastAPI request object is inferred in JS.
Direct numeric limit/version Zod fields require integer/lower bounds; this is a narrower explicit field policy, not a claim of arbitrary ordinal prose parsing.
Maintained test prose is now banned while executable directives/legal/type contracts stay intact.
Maintained JS shared-mutable default/reference controls own native forms; Pydantic default_factory has no shared Zod lifecycle.
Existing caller-before-private-helper control.
Equivalent upsert/update ownership requires schema, transaction and method semantics. Matching JavaScript method names is insufficient for a safe source rule.
Single-read/bulk-read equivalence needs driver error/order/authorization contracts; a generic JS get/getMany spelling rule would reject valid APIs.
Existing supported embedded replay-insert review is narrower than every Python store/fixture insert; raw SQL engine owns standalone replay policy.
Per-field persistence commands can express different authorization/atomicity contracts; their Python store architecture is not inferred from arbitrary JS method prefixes.
Popen.kill/wait and asyncio process.wait are Python APIs. Node uses close/exit event listeners and detached process policies; no wait-method spelling copy is sound.
Enabled maintained upstream missing-oracle detection at warning with strict/application configuration regression tests.
A deterministic cursor order requires query/order-key uniqueness evidence and database dialect. Existing no-offset-pagination remains the supported generic embedded SQL control.
Typed outcome contracts and exhaustiveness already have source owners; arbitrary joined exception strings can be user-facing messages.
Existing unused/unnecessary parameter controls own supported JS helper options; callback/contextual APIs are preserved.

HTTPX client ownership is Python-specific. Native fetch does not allocate an HTTPX client; SDK constructor allocation requires provider-specific lifetime evidence. Existing service-contract controls cover dependency boundaries, without claiming equivalent client-lifetime enforcement.
Existing declared interface consumption plus source-proven fixture reuse; no ABC is invented from a class name.
General maintained-test prose policy with legal/directive/type-contract preservation and whitespace-preserving safe fix.
Known static field reads on open Zod parser outputs require focused object schemas; opaque JSON forwarding/storage remains valid.
Explicit lower-bounded integer schema fields and validated URL numeric coercion; FastAPI annotations are not duplicated.
Object shorthand single-use renames cover the portable JS binding case. Same-name tuple attribute unpacking has no exact JS tuple assignment equivalent; snapshots remain valid.
Direct declared mutable object input writes in result-returning functions now have an explicit counterpart.

Bulk-first service design is useful when a declared application contract requires it. The Python rule enforces a suffix/CRUD convention and visible one-item/context delegation, but explicitly does not prove batching, result projection, authorization or atomicity. Existing TypeScript SQL owners support differing native operation names, while declared service interfaces may validly expose only singleton operations. No equivalent TypeScript bulk contract is established here; a generic Service/Store/Repository get/getMany naming rule would invent one.

updates.head: cba7ffff8548ea30f00cd1c8a9229cd856f2e9c8
updates.basis: All original 206 descriptor identities and implementation blobs are unchanged in this update. SARJ556 adds a separately reviewed bulk-first architecture policy; no TypeScript contract or generic CRUD-name detector is invented.

updates.head: 42a984130ef5479a9590f24095ff944193191062
updates.basis: Reviewed PostgreSQL execution ownership, grouped JOIN/read-stage accounting, parser privacy/recursion, Pydantic rejection callbacks, and runtime record/metadata identity changes. The 207 rule IDs and existing applicability decisions remain unchanged. Shared SQL analytics ownership and bounded TypeScript variant/return/exhaustiveness guidance are retained without claiming equivalent embedded-query, exception or nullable-prefix enforcement.

updates.head: 8be04fdae02f3c6e77009ce100d4c39ded3936b6
updates.basis: Reviewed imported and awaited raw-mapping return provenance, captured-source and per-file proof budgets, runtime import identity, ambiguous module ownership, and reachable borrowed aliases after nested terminal branches. Two direct-rule changes only specialize AST iteration. The existing 207 applicability decisions remain bounded: focused JSON schemas do not imply a general Map.get ban or identical imported-parser enforcement. Incoming TypeScript minimal-consumer support removes only unread required direct primitive/nullish fields under its existing private-consumer and caller proofs; named contracts, inspected nullable fields, unsafe callers and type observations retain their boundaries. Native runtime bans and upstream advisory checks add no Python registry IDs or new TypeScript ports.
